Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Sri Lanka Women's reply! The umpires are punctual and so are the Pakistan Women players who take their respective fielding positions. It is the usual opening pair of Vishmi Gunarathne and Chamari Athapaththu for Sri Lanka Women. Diana Baig will get the proceedings underway with the ball. And, here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, after a dominant performance with the ball, Sri Lanka Women would like to replicate the same when they come out to chase a below run-a-ball target. There's no visible dew however as of now, and if it remains the same, the Pakistan Women bowlers could also become effective. However, on a slow deck like this, Fatima Sana Khan's contribution towards the backend could well be the difference if their bowlers hit the right areas and utilize the conditions to their benefit. It is all about adapting to the conditions well. A riveting chase is on the cards. Stay tuned.

Anushka Sanjeewani, the Lankan keeper is down for a quick chat. She says that she is really happy with her performance and reckons that it is a good pitch. Adds that the bowlers adjusted well to the pitch and says that they are happy to chase this total. Mentions that she is really happy to see the Sri Lankan supporters and goes on to thank them as well.

The Sri Lankan bowling attack operated as a well-oiled machine, with each bowler making significant contributions and utilizing the conditions to perfection. There was no visible dew which allowed the tweakers to get in handy. Their relentless precision and tactical bowling kept the wickets tumbling at regular intervals, never allowing Pakistan to gain a foothold in the game. Sri Lanka Women were not only good with the ball through and through but the bowling changes were effective as well. Athapaththu herself was the most successful bowler with a spectacular 3-wicket haul along with Sugandika Kumari and Udeshika Prabodani too, ending up with identical number of wickets.

Fatima Sana Khan though, played a brave knock and propelled Pakistan Women to get past the triple figures somehow. Although she lacked partners from the other end, she tried to effectively weather the storm single-handedly. But, fairly to say, the early loss of wickets put the entire batting order, especially the middle order under tremendous pressure and they just couldn't recover from the collapse.

Pakistan Women's batting struggles resurfaced once again, leading to a sluggish powerplay and the early loss of their top three batters. The first half of their innings was painfully slow, with batters struggling to time the ball effectively. Although Nida Dar and Omaima Sohail attempted to build a partnership and ease the pressure, they couldn't sustain it for long. Wickets continued to fall at regular intervals, further hampering Pakistan's progress and they slipped badly from 32/3 at 6 overs to a precarious 89/8 in the 16th over.

A job well-done with the ball by the Sri Lanka Women. From the first over, till the final delivery, they have delivered a solid performance, collectively as a bowling unit. Pakistan Women on the other hand, would be disappointed as they just couldn't find any momentum through and through.

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match proceedings and it is now time to get the play underway. The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of Sri Lanka Women. It will be the duo of Muneeba Ali Siddiqi and Gull Feroza to open the innings for Pakistan Women. Udeshika Prabodani has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of the match but it is now time for the teams to step out and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Sri Lanka first, followed by the national anthem of Pakistan.

PITCH REPORT - Lisa Sthalekar and Stacy-Ann King are pitchside. They say that the surface looks a bit stiff and compacted. The spinners would be able to cash out from the track if they bowl fuller. The dimensions are pretty big in the stadium, especially the square but the leg side of a right-handed batter is the shortest of all from where they are standing.

Chamari Athapaththu, the captain of Sri Lanka Women says that it is a fresh game and they need to start afresh as well. Adds that they would have bowled first anyway, so, she is happy. Reckons that they have played good cricket over the last few months and want to continue in the same way. Informs that they have a good group of players and all the experienced players are in the team.

The skipper of Pakistan Women, Fatima Sana Khan wins the toss and opts to put a total on the board. She continues that they have watched Bangladesh's batting inning and they would like to execute the same. She is also confident after playing a couple of warm-up games and reckons that they are ready for the matchup.

Sri Lanka Women (Playing XI) - Vishmi Gunarathne, Chamari Athapaththu (C), Harshitha Madhavi, Kaveesha Dilhari, Nilakshika Silva, Hasini Perera, Anushka Sanjeewani (WK), Sugandika Kumari, Inoshi Fernando, Sachini Nisansala, Udeshika Prabodani.
Pakistan Women (Playing XI) - Muneeba Ali Siddiqi (WK), Gull Feroza, Sidra Amin, Nida Dar, Aliya Riaz, Fatima Sana Khan (C), Tuba Hassan, Nashra Sundhu, Sadia Iqbal, Diana Baig, Omaima Sohail.
TOSS - Pakistan Women have won the toss and they will BAT first.

NEWS FLASH - Bangladesh Women have just beaten Scotland Women in the opening game of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup, 2024. The would-be hosts have finally won a T20 World Cup game, ending their decade of suffering and they have made it five wins out of five against Scotland Women.

On the other hand, Pakistan Women have good records in head-to-head facing Sri Lanka Women in this format. But the last time they won against them was in 2022. After that things didn't turn out to be great for the side. On top of that, their form is not quite up to the mark. They lost a T20I series against South Africa Women and both of the warm-up matches against Scotland and Bangladesh respectively. But like people say, 'Revenge is a dish best served cold', the Women in Green would give their best to seek revenge as they lost the battle against the same opposition in the semis of the Women's Asia Cup. Sadia Iqbal is the only player from the squad who has been performing consistently by picking scalps, but it's high time for the other players to pull up their socks. Stay tuned, as we are not far away from the toss and team news.

Sri Lanka Women, who just bagged their maiden Asia Cup title in July would like to keep their momentum right on the track. The top order of this side looks monstrous with the current form of Harshitha Madhavi mixing with the skipper, Chamari Athapaththu's experience. Even when the top order has a bad day on the ground, Kaveesha Dilhari from the middle order is able to anchor the inning. In the bowling unit, they have Inoshi Fernando, leading the spin department.

Hello and welcome to this auspicious day where the ICC Women's T20 World Cup, 2024 has already kicked off in fine fashion. The atmosphere is terrific in the Sharjah Cricket Stadium and the spectators are eager to start the clash between Pakistan Women and Sri Lanka Women. Sri Lanka Women are in top shape but will they be able to get better of the Women in Greens? We shall find out.
... MATCH DAY ...

In the second game in the ICC Women's T20 World Cup, 2024, we will have the Pakistan Women and Sri Lanka Women go against each other and this promises to be an intriguing encounter. With both sides eyeing a chance to challenge the formidable India Women and Australia Women for a top-two finish, a victory here is crucial! Entering the tournament, the Pakistan Women’s side sees themselves performing poorly and will focus on bouncing back. Despite their recent struggles, they secured a game against South Africa, the runners-up of the last Women’s T20 World Cup, in a 2-1 series loss. They have lost both the warm-up games against the Scotland Women and the Bangladesh Women by some margin. To claim victory in their opening match, key performances will be essential from wicketkeeper-batter Muneeba Ali and Gull Feroza in the batting department. The bowling unit, spearheaded by Sadia Iqbal and Nida Dar, must effectively contain the opposition to give Pakistan a competitive edge. The other teams in Group A are Australia Women, India Women, and New Zealand Women and if Pakistan Women want to end up in the top two, they will need to come up with something special, and they could well start that with a win in this game. On the other hand, the Sri Lankan Women too, will have to go through stiff competition in making their path to the semi-finals. They will realistically need some luck by their side as well to secure a top-two finish. Captain Chamari Athapaththu stands out as a pivotal player, bringing an elite skill level that could easily see her feature in any team in this tournament. Familiarity with the Sharjah conditions could play a pivotal role, and all eyes will be on her. Her performance will be crucial to Sri Lanka's batting success, alongside promising talents like Kavisha Dilhari and Harshitha Samarawickrama, who will need to capitalize on early innings. In the bowling department, Athapaththu is expected to contribute alongside Inoshi Priyadharshani, who will play a vital role in containing runs and taking wickets to ensure competitive totals. Together, the top order and bowling attack will be critical to Sri Lanka's aspirations in the tournament. So, which side will secure the first points in their campaign? We shall find out together.
